claims.text: Adding approximately 0.2–0.5 wt% yttrium during fabrication of NiCoCrAlY-based bond coats will improve coating durability.
The yttrium addition will improve coating reliability.
The yttrium addition will enhance oxide-scale adherence.
Yttrium doping will promote formation of a finely grained Al2O3 scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be adherent.
Yttrium will segregate to oxide grain boundaries.
Segregation of yttrium to oxide grain boundaries will reduce interfacial strain.
Reduced interfacial strain will improve adhesion of the thermally grown oxide.
Yttrium doping will retard rapid oxide-scale growth.
Yttrium doping will retard oxide-scale spallation.
Yttrium-doped coatings will have greater oxidation resistance than the untreated baseline.
Yttrium-doped coatings will exhibit less oxide spallation than the untreated baseline.
The proposed improvement will remain effective under oxidative thermal cycling at approximately 1000–1200 °C.
Uniform distribution of yttrium during fabrication is required for the predicted improvement.
The untreated NiCoCrAlY-based baseline contains no reactive-element doping.

contradictions.description: The baseline is called NiCoCrAlY while also being described as lacking reactive-element or yttrium doping. The 'Y' in NiCoCrAlY conventionally denotes yttrium, so it is unclear whether the intervention introduces yttrium into a Y-free NiCoCrAl composition or increases the yttrium content of an already Y-containing alloy.
